items.text: $X$ quasi-compact, $Y\subset X$ closed irreducible: there is a minimal closed irreducible $Y'\subset Y$ (Zorn: $\bigcap Y_\alpha\neq\varnothing$ for a chain, by quasi-compactness).
Y\ \text{minimal closed irreducible}\iff Y=\overline{\{y\}}\ \ \forall y\in Y,\ Y\neq\varnothing
$X$ sober: the minimal closed irreducible subsets are the closed points. $X$ sober and quasi-compact: every closed subset has a closed point.
$X$ Noetherian: every increasing sequence of open subsets is stationary.
X\ \text{Noetherian}\iff\text{every open subset of }X\text{ is quasi-compact}
A\ \text{Noetherian ring}\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Spec}A\ \text{Noetherian space}\quad(\text{decreasing closed sets}\leftrightarrow\text{increasing radical ideals})
$X$ Noetherian space: the set of irreducible components is finite. ($A$ Noetherian: finitely many minimal primes.)

Noetherian induction: a nonempty family of closed subsets has a minimal element. If $Y$ is minimal with infinitely many components, it is not irreducible, $Y=Y'\cup Y''$ with $Y',Y''\subsetneq Y$, one of them has infinitely many: contradiction.
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ for $A$ of finite type over a field $k$
X(k)\ \subset\ X_0=\operatorname{Max}(A)\ \subset\ \operatorname{Spec}A;\qquad X(k)=\{\mathfrak M : \kappa(\mathfrak M)=k\},\ \ X(k)=X_0\ \text{if }k=\bar k
$X_0\subset X$ is very dense if $U\mapsto U\cap X_0$ is injective on open sets.
X_0\ \text{very dense}\iff\text{every nonempty locally closed }Z\subset X\text{ meets }X_0\iff T\cap X_0\ \text{dense in }T\ \ \forall\,T\ \text{closed}
Then $\mathcal O(X)\simeq\mathcal O(X_0)$ and $\operatorname{Top}(X)\simeq\operatorname{Top}(X_0)$; if $X$ is sober, $X$ is the sober space associated to $X_0$ (closed irreducible subsets of $X_0$).
A\ \text{of finite type over a field}:\qquad \text{the closed points are dense in every closed }Y\subset X
For topology (sheaves, components, closed sets) one may replace $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by $X(k)$, $k=\bar k$; generic points are lost.
